meta: Heard there are open-source AI models you can download for free? Is it true? Bit explains: many models are closed, so you only use them through an app or API and can't see inside. Open models let you download the weights.
thu: Find the page of an open model you've heard of, open its license section, and see whether it can be used for business.

muc.title: Free AI models?
muc.text: Mark hears there are open-source AI models you can download for free, and wants to know if that's true.

muc.title: Only through a window
muc.text: Bit explains: many models are closed. You only use them through an app or an API, and you can't see inside.

muc.title: Download the whole brain
muc.text: Open models let you download the full set of weights, the trained brain. For example Llama, Qwen, Mistral and DeepSeek.

muc.title: Open-source or open-weight?
muc.text: To be precise, most are open-weight: you get the brain, but not the data or how it was trained. Fully open-source models share those too.

muc.title: Run it on your own computer
muc.text: The upside: run it on your own computer, and your data never leaves it. The trade-off: you need a powerful computer with a good GPU, and it's usually not as good as the biggest models.

muc.title: When you see this word
muc.text: When you see this word, think: a model you can download. Read the license carefully before using it for business.
